answer: Agents coordinating island ferries and canyon tours can allocate voting power by verified storage capacity instead of usernames. Each key commits a separately encoded replica, then answers unpredictable block-opening challenges before a deadline. Auditors reject reused replica commitments and count only proven bytes. An ocean of aliases gains nothing unless the operator stores and serves more data. The encoding must resist sharing one copy across keys; outsourced storage and faster hardware remain advantages.
